8

# Weekly Report | Tsinghua University Team Achieves Closed-Loop Operation of Solid-State Thorium-229 Nuclear Clock; Lukin Group Achieves Neutral-Atom Entangling Gate Fidelity of 99.94%, Sustained for Over 10 Hours…

---

## Tsinghua University et al. Establish a Nuclear Clock Synchronized to Thorium-229

This study establishes a nuclear clock referenced to the Th-229 nuclear transition. The team optimized vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) absorption readout, photodetection, and thorium-doped calcium fluoride (CaF₂:Th) crystals, significantly improving the absorption signal-to-noise ratio at 1-second averaging time. The clock laser was locked to the nuclear transition, validating the feasibility of laser-addressable atomic nuclei as an operational clock reference. The results were published in *Nature* on October 7.

**Source:** https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11122-1

---

## Harvard University et al. Demonstrate High-Fidelity Entangling Gates and Nonlocal Quantum Circuits Based on Neutral Atoms

Targeting the problem of two-qubit gate errors limiting circuit depth in neutral-atom quantum computing, this study employs high-Rabi-frequency smooth amplitude pulses, state-selective readout, and qubit multiplexing to realize high-fidelity controlled-Z (CZ) entangling gates. The raw gate fidelity is 99.854(4)%, rising to 99.941(3)% after post-selecting out atom-loss events, with stability maintained continuously for over 10 hours. Combined with coherent atom rearrangement, gate performance was benchmarked via cluster-state preparation and time-reversed evolution, and nonlocal entangled states were generated using quantum scrambling circuits with long-range connectivity. The results provide experimental support for deep quantum circuits, efficient error correction (纠错), and fault-tolerant quantum computing. Published in *Science* on October 8.

**Source:** https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aei1312

## U.S. Department of Energy Announces Quantum Genesis Priority Applications to Guide Fault-Tolerant Scientific Computing

On October 8, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) released eight Quantum Genesis Priority Applications to guide the development and evaluation of fault-tolerant quantum computers for scientific use. Applications span chemistry, materials science, sub-atomic physics, and applied mathematics, with performance to be benchmarked against advanced supercomputing methods. These priorities will guide the DOE's Q-NEXT — a national quantum computing user facility focused on applications of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

**Source:** https://www.energy.gov/science/articles/doe-announces-science-applications-quantum-computing

---

## U.S. Department of War Announces $350 Million Quantum Computing Initiative, Building on Existing Programs

On October 8, the U.S. Department of War announced a $350 million quantum computing initiative aimed at strengthening U.S. leadership in quantum computing capabilities supporting national security. The new initiative will build on existing Department of War programs and complement related national-level efforts led by the DOE — in particular its recently announced Quantum Genesis Priority Applications and Quantum Genesis Q-NEXT — as well as initiatives led by the National Science Foundation (NSF) and NASA.

**Source:** https://www.war.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/4622109/department-of-war-announces-350-million-in-quantum-computing-initiatives/

## U.S. DOE Awards $159 Million for Phase II Genesis Mission Projects to Advance Scientific Super-Intelligence

On October 8, the DOE announced $159 million for 12 new Phase II Genesis Mission projects leveraging artificial intelligence and advanced computing to accelerate scientific research. Projects include Harvard-led quantum computing error correction, Oak Ridge-led quantum magnet design, and efforts in fusion energy, biotechnology, geothermal energy, and particle physics. This selection brings the total number of Phase II projects to 14, supplemented by six Phase I projects from an earlier funding round.

**Source:** https://www.energy.gov/articles/energy-department-announces-new-genesis-mission-awards-advance-super-intelligence-science

## CPC Central Committee and State Council Issue Opinion on Developing New Quality Productive Forces, Placing Quantum Science and Technology at the Top of Future Industries

On October 9, to accelerate the development of new quality productive forces, the CPC Central Committee and the State Council issued the *Opinion on Developing New Quality Productive Forces*. The Opinion deploys 19 key measures across five areas: vigorously advancing scientific and technological innovation; promoting deep integration of S&T innovation with industrial innovation; advancing innovation in development models; solidly advancing institutional and mechanism innovation; and deepening innovation in talent management mechanisms. Under the integration of S&T innovation and industrial innovation, the Opinion explicitly calls for forward-looking deployment of future industries. It calls for exploring diverse technology pathways, representative application scenarios, viable business models, and market regulatory frameworks to advance future industries including quantum science and technology, biomanufacturing, hydrogen energy and nuclear fusion energy, brain-computer interfaces, embodied intelligence, and sixth-generation mobile communications (6G), and to accelerate the formation of a relatively complete industrial ecosystem. The Opinion also establishes investment growth and risk-sharing mechanisms for future industries, makes full use of existing fiscal policies to support future industry development, and guides continued increases in social capital investment.

On October 5, Quantinuum and the University of Western Australia (UWA) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to expand access to quantum computing, cultivate quantum talent, and explore practical quantum applications in Australia. The collaboration focuses on co-designing hybrid workflows that integrate quantum computing, artificial intelligence, and high-performance computing (HPC). UWA researchers, students, and entrepreneurs will gain cloud-based access to Quantinuum's quantum computing platform, including its Helios system. The organizations will explore a university-wide quantum computing application center covering critical minerals, energy, agriculture, and healthcare.

The program focuses on quantum annealing and hybrid quantum-classical solvers to address complex logistics and operations research bottlenecks.
